newsitem.title: FINLAND: UN rights envoy says civil war danger over Kosovo.
newsitem.headline: UN rights envoy says civil war danger over Kosovo.

text.p: U.N. human rights investigator Elisabeth Rehn said on Tuesday that political conflict and violence in Serbia's Albanian-majority province of Kosovo could lead to civil war.

Kosovo, whose limited autonomy was revoked in 1989 to quell agitation by its 90 percent Albanian majority for more self-rule and to protect minority Serbs, has been shaken by renewed, sporadic anti-Serb violence in the past year.
Rehn said that if Serbia's political crisis spread to Kosovo "it can be a real explosion, a fire," adding: "We can fear anything, even civil war."

Rehn told a news conference in Helsinki that she would ask Belgrade for permission to open a U.N. human rights office in Pristina, Kosovo's main city, to improve the international presence there. Kosovo borders Albania.

"A new conflict is emerging here ... which is taking Albania maybe even towards civil war, and this is truly alarming," Rehn said. "Unfortunately Europe has not been on its toes enough. The United States on the other hand has understood how sensitive the situation there really is."

Serbian government officials were due to meet Serbian opposition members and ethnic Albanians on Tuesday in Germany to discuss the future status of Kosovo, where a car bomb attack last week injured the Serb rector of the university in Pristina.
Belgrade newspapers have reported that Serb nationalists had decided to retaliate against Albanians if attacks continued.
Serbs regard Kosovo, where they fought a 14th-century battle against the Turks, as the cradle of their culture.
Rehn said she feared attempts to take political advantage of violence against the minority Serbs in Kosovo.

"Kosovo is the place where everything started in 1987 when (Serbian President Slobodan) Milosevic held his famous speech 'You Serbs will not be beaten any longer' which started his rise to power and started the whole conflict situation," she said.
"I am now afraid that this could again be taken advantage of."
Milosevic used attacks on Kosovo Serbs to help centralise and concentrate power in his hands in the late 1980s.
